title: Quantum machine learning models for graphs
authors: Frédéric Sauvage, Pranav Kalidindi, Frederic Rapp, Martın Larocca
abstract: Geometric Machine Learning (GML) successes have been achieved through the thorough study and design of new equivariant neural networks. In comparison, geometric quantum machine learning (GQML) models lack such a detailed understanding and, despite already several proposals, a unifying perspective on their design remains elusive. In this work, we focus on GQML models for graph problems that showcase a lot of structure and still remain frontier in machine learning. For the case when n-node graphs are encoded in n-qubit states, we provide a comprehensive characterization of their constituents. Taken together, these furnish us with a toolbox for the design of quantum graph models, and we further probe its benefits including the natural integration with classical models, generalization of known GQML models (sometimes extending their expressivity at virtually no cost), and straightforward classical pre-training strategies. The latter two features are demonstrated in dedicated numerical experiments.
summary: This paper establishes a comprehensive mathematical framework—a 'toolbox'—for designing Geometric Quantum Machine Learning (GQML) models tailored for graph structures. By rigorously enforcing symmetry constraints derived from the permutation group $S_n$, it provides systematic methods to construct, characterize, and improve the expressivity of quantum circuits used in quantum machine learning tasks.
main_problem: The work aims to develop a rigorous framework for Geometric Quantum Machine Learning (GQML) models applied to graph problems, addressing the lack of a unifying design perspective compared to classical GML.
main_result: A comprehensive 'toolbox' is provided to systematically characterize and construct equivariant quantum graph models, demonstrating benefits like natural integration with classical methods and enabling classical pre-training strategies.
method: The authors employ group theory (specifically the permutation group $S_n$) to define equivariance/invariance for quantum operators and maps, leading to a systematic basis construction via symmetrization (twirling).

main_assumptions: The analysis relies on defining equivariance with respect to group actions ($S_n$) and assumes that model expressivity can be systematically increased by incorporating all compatible equivariant observables.

why_interesting: This work provides a deep theoretical grounding in symmetry principles (group representation theory) applied directly to quantum computation models for structured data like graphs, which is highly relevant for designing physically constrained quantum circuits.
